Spring 5/6/7 Spring's AOP, transaction management, security, and caching all work through proxies — wrapper objects that intercept method calls and inject cross-cutting behaviour before or after the real method executes. How a Proxy Works

When a bean is eligible for proxying (it has an aspect, a @Transactional method, etc.), Spring replaces the bean in the application context with a proxy object . Callers receive the proxy, not the real object. Every method call goes through the proxy's interception chain before reaching the target.
How JDK Dynamic Proxy Works

JDK Dynamic Proxies are part of the Java standard library ( java.lang.reflect.Proxy ). They work by creating a new class at runtime that implements one or more interfaces . 5. Spring Boot DevTools — Hot Reload

DevTools monitors the JVM classpath for changes and triggers a fast restart — not a full JVM restart. It keeps the JVM alive, swaps only the application's own classes (the app classloader), and restarts the Spring context. This typically takes 1–3 seconds vs 5–20 seconds for a cold start.
Add to pom.xml

<!-- pom.xml -->
<dependency>
    <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
    <artifactId>spring-boot-devtools</artifactId>
    <scope>runtime</scope>
    <optional>true</optional>
</dependency>
application.properties

# Enable classpath watcher and restart on change
spring.devtools.restart.enabled=true

# Enable LiveReload server (port 35729) — browser extension triggers refresh
spring.devtools.livereload.enabled=true
